**although / even though / though** + пі:
**although / even though / though** + subject + verb — at the start or in the middle of the sentence
**despite / in spite of** + noun / pronoun / -ing · *despite the fact that* + clause
**However, / Nevertheless,** — at the start of a new sentence; or inside it: *The flat, **however**, is great.*
**whereas / while** — between two parts, with a comma: *A, whereas B.*
**though** at the end — only in speech: *It was worth it, **though**.*
**despite / in spite of** + іменник / V-: **despite / in spite of** + noun / V-ing · despite **the fact that** + clause
However / Nevertheless — на початку друг: However / Nevertheless — at the start of the second sentence; nevertheless is more formal.
However with a comma starts a new sentence.
However не з'єднує частини одного реченн: However doesn't join the parts of one sentence with a comma.
It was a long flight. I slept most of th: It was a long flight. I slept most of the way, ___. (spoken “but still” at the end)
___ I've lived here for years, I still g: ___ I've lived here for years, I still get lost in the Old Town. (even if it's true that, 2 words)
___ the fact that he's rich, he's very m: ___ the fact that he's rich, he's very modest. (one word)
although / even though + підмет і дієсло: although / even though + subject and verb; even though is stronger.
but joins the parts of one sentence.
despite / in spite of + іменник або -ing: despite / in spite of + noun or -ing — shorter than a whole clause.
however не з'єднує два речення через ком: however doesn't join two sentences with a comma like but: you need a full stop and a comma after however.
however починає нове речення; ставити йо: however starts a new sentence; putting it after a comma instead of but is a mistake.
in spite — завжди з of, а despite — без: in spite — always with of, but despite — without of.
though в кінці речення — м'яке «але» до: though at the end of a sentence — a soft “but” about what was said before.
though у кінці речення — розмовне «утім»: though at the end of a sentence — spoken “but still”.
whereas / while — люди чи речі відрізняю: whereas / while — people or things are different, nothing happens “against expectations”.
«Хоча… але» — англійською лише одне з дв: In English you use only one word, not “although… but”.
It was cheap. However, it was good.
Готель був трохи старий. Утім, персонал: The hotel was a bit old. However, the staff were great.
Два різні факти поруч: Two different facts side by side
Квартира досить маленька. Проте розташув: The flat is quite small. However, the location is perfect.
Квартира маленька. Проте вона зовсім пор: The flat is small. However, it's right next to the station.
The concert at the Lviv Opera was expensive. However, it was worth every penny.
Олівер любить поїздки до міст, а Емма ві: Oliver loves city trips, but Emma prefers the countryside.
Перед іменником — despite або in spite o: Before a noun — despite or in spite of.
We were tired, but we still went to the party.
Попри затори, ми вчасно дісталися до аер: There were traffic jams, but we still got to the airport on time.
Попри те що Анна живе в Лондоні вже три: Anna has lived in London for three years, but she still gets lost on the Underground.
Попри те що погано почувалася, Оксана пі: Oksana felt ill, but she still went to work.
Попри холод, ми поплавали в Чорному морі: It was cold, but we still swam in the Black Sea.
Just two different facts side by side.
Після **despite** не буває ні *of*, ні р: After **despite** there is no *of* and no clause: ~~despite it was raining~~ → *despite **the rain*** or *despite **the fact that** it was raining*.
After although comes a full clause.
Після despite речення ставимо лише через: After despite, a clause comes only with the fact that.
Після despite — іменник (her cold); alth: After despite — a noun (her cold); although and even though need a full clause, whereas compares two facts.
Після despite — іменник, -ing або the fa: After despite — a noun, -ing or the fact that.
Хоча було холодно, ми поплавали в Чорном: It was cold, but we still swam in the Black Sea.
Хоча квартира маленька, нам вона подобає: The flat is small, but we like it.
Хоча ми забронювали столик, нам довелося: We had booked a table, but we still had to wait twenty minutes.
I was tired, but I still finished the book.
Хоча я поставив два будильники, я проспа: I set two alarms, but I still overslept.
Ці слова кажуть «хоча / попри / проте»,: These words all mean “although / despite / however”, but each one needs its own grammar. Choose by what comes next — a whole clause, a noun or a new sentence — and by style: speech or writing.
I drink tea, and my brother drinks coffee.
I'm an early bird, but Emma is a night owl.
